note.text:
To read the coordinates of a point, start at the origin O. Count along the x-axis to below or above the point: that is the abscissa (positive to the right, negative to the left). Then count up or down to the point: that is the ordinate (positive up, negative down).
To plot a point, for example (−3, 2): from O go 3 units left, then 2 units up.
Moving a point right adds to the abscissa; left subtracts. Moving up adds to the ordinate; down subtracts.
Two points with the same ordinate are on a horizontal line: their distance is the difference of their abscissas. (−2, 3) and (4, 3) are 4 − (−2) = 6 units apart.

worked_example.problem: Start at the point A{pt(x, y)}. Move {r} units to the right, then {d} units down. What are the coordinates of the new point B?
steps: Moving right adds to the abscissa: {x} + {r} = {x + r}.
Moving down subtracts from the ordinate: {y} − {d} = {y - d}.
worked_example.figure: coordPlane([['A', x, y], ['B', x + r, y - d]])

cards.idea: To read a point: from O, count along the x-axis first (the abscissa), then up or down (the ordinate).
example: P is {a} units right and {b} units up from O, so P = {pt(a, b)}.

cards.idea: Left of the y-axis the abscissa is negative; below the x-axis the ordinate is negative.
example: Q is {-a} units left and {-b} units down from O, so Q = {pt(a, b)}.

cards.idea: Two points with the same ordinate are on a horizontal line. Their distance is the larger abscissa minus the smaller.
example: {pt(a, y)} and {pt(b, y)}: {b} − {br(a)} = {b - a} units apart.

cards.idea: Moving a point right or left changes only the abscissa. Moving it up or down changes only the ordinate.
example: {pt(x, y)} moved {r} units right: {pt(x + r, y)}.
{pt(x, y)} moved {r} units down: {pt(x, y - r)}.

check.prompt: Start at {pt(x, y)} and move {plural(r, 'unit', 'units')} to the {right ? 'right' : 'left'}. Where are you?

distractors.text: {pt(right ? x + r : x - r, right ? y + r : y - r)}

misconceptions.explain: Moving {right ? 'right' : 'left'} changes the abscissa, not the ordinate.
{right ? 'Right adds to the abscissa' : 'Left subtracts from the abscissa'}.
Only the abscissa changes: the ordinate stays {y}.

solution: Moving {right ? 'right adds' : 'left subtracts'} {r} to the abscissa; the ordinate stays {y}.

questions.prompt: What are the coordinates of point P?

misconceptions.explain: The abscissa (along) comes first, then the ordinate (up or down).
P is {x > 0 ? 'right' : 'left'} of the y-axis, so its abscissa is {x > 0 ? 'positive' : 'negative'}.
P is {y > 0 ? 'above' : 'below'} the x-axis, so its ordinate is {y > 0 ? 'positive' : 'negative'}.

solution: From O, P is {abs(x)} units {x > 0 ? 'right' : 'left'} and {abs(y)} units {y > 0 ? 'up' : 'down'}.

misconceptions.explain: {N[1]} is at {pt(y, x)}: the numbers are the other way round. Go along first, then up or down.
{N[2]} is at {pt(-x, y)}: it is on the other side of the y-axis.
{N[3]} is at {pt(x, -y)}: it is on the other side of the x-axis.

solution: {pt(x, y)}: from O go {abs(x)} units {x > 0 ? 'right' : 'left'}, then {abs(y)} units {y > 0 ? 'up' : 'down'}.

questions.prompt: A = {pt(a, y)} and B = {pt(b, y)}. How many units apart are A and B?

misconceptions.explain: Count the units from A to B across the y-axis: {b} − {br(a)} = {b - a}.

solution: A and B have the same ordinate, {y}, so they are on a horizontal line.

questions.prompt: C = {pt(x, a)} and D = {pt(x, b)}. How many units apart are C and D?

misconceptions.explain: Count the units from C to D across the x-axis: {b} − {br(a)} = {b - a}.

solution: C and D have the same abscissa, {x}, so they are on a vertical line.

questions.prompt: Start at A{pt(x, y)}. Move {plural(r, 'unit', 'units')} to the {right ? 'right' : 'left'} and {plural(u, 'unit', 'units')} {up ? 'up' : 'down'}. Where are you?
questions.correct: {pt(right ? x + r : x - r, up ? y + u : y - u)}

distractors.text: {pt(right ? x - r : x + r, up ? y + u : y - u)}
{pt(right ? x + r : x - r, up ? y - u : y + u)}
{pt(up ? y + u : y - u, right ? x + r : x - r)}

misconceptions.explain: {right ? 'Right adds to' : 'Left subtracts from'} the abscissa.
{up ? 'Up adds to' : 'Down subtracts from'} the ordinate.
The abscissa comes first in the ordered pair.

questions.prompt: A{pt(a, b)}, B{pt(c, b)} and C{pt(c, d)} are three corners of the rectangle ABCD. What are the coordinates of D?

misconceptions.explain: The abscissa comes first: D is level with A across, so its abscissa is {a}.
D is under or over A, so it has A's abscissa, {a}.

solution: In a rectangle with sides along the grid, D is below or above A and level with C.
D has the abscissa of A, {a}, and the ordinate of C, {d}: D = {answer}.
questions.figure: coordPlane([['A', a, b], ['B', c, b], ['C', c, d]])
